preconditions.description: The number of points n is an integer between 3 and 70 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(initial_positions) == 3 and all(1 <= p <= n for p in initial_positions) and len(set(initial_positions)) == 3
preconditions.description: The initial positions are three distinct integers between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: len(matrix) == n and all(len(row) == n for row in matrix)
preconditions.description: The color matrix is an n x n grid of characters.

preconditions.expression: all(matrix[i][j] == matrix[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(n)) and all(matrix[i][i] == '*' for i in range(n))
preconditions.description: The matrix is symmetric and the main diagonal contains '*' symbols.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c.islower() or c == '*' for c in row) for row in matrix)
preconditions.description: All non-diagonal entries in the matrix are lowercase English letters representing colors.

postconditions.description: The output is either -1 indicating impossibility, or a valid sequence of moves that achieves the goal with the minimal number of steps.
If the output starts with -1, it signifies that no sequence of moves can place stones on vertices 1, 2, and 3.
If a solution exists, the first line is the number of moves, and the subsequent lines count matches this number.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and all(move_from in current_stones and move_to not in current_stones and matrix[move_from-1][move_to-1] == color_of_other_pair(current_stones, move_from) for move_from, move_to in moves)
postconditions.description: Each move is valid: the stone moves from an occupied vertex to a free vertex, and the diagonal color matches the color of the diagonal connecting the other two stones.
After executing all moves, the stones occupy exactly vertices 1, 2, and 3.
The number of moves in the solution is the minimum possible number of moves required to reach the target configuration.
